records.title: Finite-fibre computable-randomness preservation versus endomorphism prior art
records.exact_target: For each fixed k>=1, everywhere-total computable fair-coin-preserving Cantor self-maps F with |F^{-1}(y)|<=k for every y; ask whether every computably random x has F(x) computably random, with no effective inverse branches, selectors or fibre enumerations assumed.
findings: SRC-0060 supplies a named unrestricted preservation framework, endomorphism randomness, over a.e.-computable measure-preserving self-maps; ordinary computable randomness is not preserved by that full class.
SRC-0061 shows everywhere-totality plus fair-coin preservation is also insufficient in general: a total truth-table functional inducing fair-coin measure can destroy computable randomness.
Neither inspected source states a finite/global bounded cardinal fibre hypothesis or an equivalent bounded-multiplicity condition.
THM-0038 preserves computable randomness only with explicit a.e.-computable inverse-pair data, which CAND-01 does not assume.
THM-0037 is reverse-direction no-randomness-from-nothing and does not imply forward conservation.

hypothesis_axes.totality: CAND-01 is everywhere total. SRC-0061 reaches everywhere-total maps; SRC-0060/SRC-0015 use a.e.-computable maps.
hypothesis_axes.fibre: CAND-01 requires a fixed global |F^{-1}(y)|<=k for every y. No inspected primary result matched this axis.
hypothesis_axes.inverse_information: CAND-01 assumes none. THM-0038 assumes an explicit a.e.-computable inverse pair; no conversion from finite cardinal fibres is inferred.
hypothesis_axes.implication_direction: CAND-01 asks forward conservation. THM-0037 is reverse existential preimage existence; THM-0071/THM-0072 are forward non-conservation results for broader map classes.

adjacent_terminology: truth-table functional = total Turing functional in SRC-0061
endomorphism = a.e.-computable measure-preserving self-morphism in SRC-0060
uniformly p-to-one endomorphism / finite-to-one factor / bounded-to-one are established classical dynamics terms but no exact computable-randomness theorem was located in this bounded attack
records.novelty_guard: No openness or novelty conclusion is inferred from search absence. The exact finite-fibre restriction remains unresolved under the evidence inspected.

records.title: Everywhere-total nonergodic effective-open Birkhoff convergence versus existing effective ergodic theory
records.exact_target: On fair-coin Cantor space, for every everywhere-total computable fair-coin-preserving self-map T and every effectively open U, require the one-sided averages N^{-1} sum_{i<N} 1_U(T^i(x)) to converge. No ergodicity, equality to lambda(U), computability of lambda(U), convergence modulus or rate is required.
findings: SRC-0058 is the closest characterization framework: nonergodic convergence-only is exact, but its computable measure-preserving transformations are a.e.-defined rather than everywhere total; its Martin-Löf converse uses computable observables/sets, while its lower-semicomputable extension is one-way weak-2 sufficiency.
SRC-0062 strengthens the nonergodic lower-semicomputable sufficiency side to Oberwolfach randomness for computable measures, while explicitly stating that T is not assumed total.
SRC-0057 directly treats effectively-open indicators and lower-semicomputable observables, but assumes ergodicity and concludes equality with the expectation.

SRC-0063 supplies total computable Cantor maps and effectively-open indicator equality, but only inside computable ergodic group actions by automorphisms with Folner averaging, not arbitrary one-sided self-map iterates.

No inspected primary theorem states the exact CAND-02 combination of everywhere-total arbitrary fair-coin-preserving self-maps, effectively-open indicators, no ergodicity and convergence-only characterization semantics.

hypothesis_axes.totality: CAND-02 is everywhere total. SRC-0058 and SRC-0062 use a.e./non-total operators. SRC-0063 uses total Cantor maps but only as an automorphism group action.
hypothesis_axes.observable_effectivity: CAND-02 uses effectively-open indicators. THM-0059 and THM-0074 directly use effectively open events; THM-0064 and THM-0073 use the broader lower-semicomputable observable class.
hypothesis_axes.ergodicity: CAND-02 has no ergodicity hypothesis. THM-0063, THM-0064 and THM-0073 are nonergodic; THM-0059, THM-0060 and THM-0074 require ergodicity.
hypothesis_axes.conclusion_strength: CAND-02 asks for existence of the one-sided Birkhoff limit only, with no equality-to-expectation and no modulus. The nonergodic sources preserve convergence-only semantics; the ergodic sources state the stronger equality conclusion.
hypothesis_axes.averaging_scheme: CAND-02 uses one-sided iterates of an arbitrary self-map. SRC-0063 uses amenable-group Folner averages, so its total/effectively-open match does not erase this structural mismatch.

adjacent_terminology: weak Birkhoff = convergence-only terminology in SRC-0058
lower semicomputable observable subsumes bounded effectively-open indicators on the observable axis
computable transformation/operator is not uniform terminology for totality across the inspected sources
computable Cantor group action in SRC-0063 supplies total maps but adds automorphism/action and Folner structure
records.novelty_guard: No openness or novelty conclusion is inferred from search absence. The exact everywhere-total/nonergodic/effectively-open characterization remains unresolved under the evidence inspected.
